name: VPS and dev boxes
ownerWords: stop being paranoid in plan under p45, p221. these should be modeled separately, like in a doc tracking all the known vps infra risks and a duty that checks these. ... things are meant to be first written in plan -> achieved -> cleared & written on duty for maintanence only -> and valiantly persued whenever not met. JUST DO IT
goal: No risk on the infra risk page (wiki domains/ops/infra-risks, its list in duties/01a11af8-962e-773d-a19a-ee4104011987/infra-risks.json) has a Grafana alert rule firing, every disk on us-metal01 and us-metal02 has at least 30 days left at the rate its Grafana rule reads (the 24 h trend, the loss over the last 24 h on /hdd.raid10, the 7 d trend on /drive2), all 9 M1 Air runners are online, and no OOM kill hits us-metal01 or us-metal02 in 24 h outside a scope of the heavy wrapper that no fix step explains. On 10-19 disk_days_min replaced root_disk_days, because a filling disk came back 9 times across us-metal01's /, /ci and /hdd.raid10 and us-metal02's /, and root_disk_days read only us-metal01's / (51 days while us-metal02's / read 6.9). On 10-19 oom_kills_24h took over the hold of p456, after us-metal02 had 40 OOM kills from 13:14Z to 16:52Z. On 10-20 explainedKills started naming the fix step that explains each box's kills up to a time, and oom_kills_24h counts only the kills after it (p468), because p456's fixed kills held the number at 41 for a whole day. On 10-21 /hdd.raid10 moved from the 24 h trend to its loss over the last 24 h, because it changes in one OpenSearch snapshot step a night: from 10-18 to 10-21 it lost 269, 328 and 514 GB a night while its 24 h trend read 9 to 739 GB a day and its old 7 d rule rate 81 to 169. Tell the owner only when a risk fires with no fix moving it. On 10-20 alerts_firing moved to the run detail to keep one headline and 3 more: the alert bridge already gives each firing rule routed to this chat its own triage job, and the rule firing on 10-19 and 10-20 (metal02-dev-disk-fill-30d) is the same fault risks_firing and disk_days_min read.

metrics.label: Risks on the infra risk page with a Grafana rule firing
Lowest days to full across every us-metal01 and us-metal02 disk at the rate its Grafana rule reads
OOM kills on us-metal01 and us-metal02 in the last 24 h outside heavy scopes and after the kills a fix step explains

onMiss: Fix a source_error first; a gap line means the risk page names a rule Grafana lacks, so fix the page's list or the rule. Each firing line names the risk page line and its owner. For each one add one fix step with duty "<dutyId>/risks_firing" naming that risk, and steer the owner's live job on it, or start one job with rlm.create_session that lands a code change for it (in auto-sns-agent through the repo's git-workflow skill 'Ship a change', plain commit.mjs on the tip, or a sieun-pi commit), and set the step's duty, job and sessionId. A risk owned by another thread gets the ask once with the page line, and this chat's fix step tracks its land. disk_days_min under 30: the flagged line names the box and disk. A us-metal01 disk gets its fix step under p448 with the metal box owner's job. us-metal02's / is this chat's own: find what grows with du on the top folders and start one job that removes or moves it. air_runners_online under 9: read devbox_runner_up by name on obs.virev.ai and bring the missing runner back on the M1 Air. oom_kills_24h over 0: each oom line names the box, its kills outside heavy scopes, about when the last kill was and the units the user journal names. heavy_scope_kills in the run detail counts the kills inside scopes of the heavy wrapper, which hit the MemoryMax their job chose; they need no step, and the job sees its own failed run. oom_kills_24h counts only the kills after the newest until of the box in explainedKills of vps-boxes.duty.json, and oom_kills_explained in the run detail counts the kills before it, named on the box's oom_explained line with its step (p456 explains every us-metal02 kill up to 16:52Z on 10-19). When a fix step lands for a new kill, add {box, until, step} to explainedKills with the time of the last kill it explains and release the file, so the fixed cause stops holding the number. Never add an entry for a kill no step fixed. For a newer kill, find the victim with journalctl --user ("killed by the OOM killer" and "oom-kill" lines) and the memory pressure around it, and add one fix step with duty "<dutyId>/oom_kills_24h" naming the box and the victim. A us-metal01 kill gets its step with the metal box owner's job (thread 01a11d24-ac9b-757d-ac51-9b2b7598782f), and a us-metal02 kill is this chat's own: stop the process with no live owner or steer the job that runs it. A line that cites /proc/vmstat means Prometheus lost node_vmstat_oom_kill, so the count runs since boot; fix the exporter first. An unchecked line is a risk with no rule; give it a rule through the Grafana alert code. The run detail's alerts_firing counts Grafana rules firing for this chat; the alert bridge's triage job holds each one, and a rule that fires on something that is not a fault gets fixed or deleted in grafana/alerting. Tell the owner which risks fire and what fixes them. All on target: no message.
